study.title: Integrating Soil Properties Into Species Distribution Models Enhances Predictive Accuracy for Terricolous Macrofungi
study.authors: Li, Rota, Peter, Gross, Scherrer, Baltensweiler
study.access: Fulltext HTML and official WSL/DORA published PDF accessed and substantive sections read. No paywall bypass. Supplementary DOCX returned HTTP403 in web and remote URL reader.
study.license: CC-BY-4.0; confirmed through Crossref license metadata, also Attribution notice on first PDF page

target: Regional habitat suitability/distribution of 162 terricolous macrofungal species in Swiss forests; presence-background modelling, not daily fruiting or probability of finding mushrooms on an outing.

study_details.taxa: 162species;51saprotrophic;111reported as ectomycorrhizal group, including109true ectomycorrhizal and2parasites
study_details.predictors: 83candidates:23climate,29topography,31soil. Species/algorithm selection of2from each class, pairwise absolute correlation below0.7.
study_details.soil: Depth, gravel, clay, sand, fine-earth density, pH, SOC. Six standard soil layers in source; analysis omitted100–200cm, retaining0–100cm.
study_details.climate: Primarily1981–2010normals at250m; growing degree days1961–1990at25m. No operational weather forecast.
study_details.background: 1000random forest background points for GLM/MAXENT, at least1kmfrom presences; RF background downsampled to presence count. Background is not surveyed absence.
study_details.validation: 5-fold cross-validation repeated20times after parameter selection; same folds used with real and randomized soil predictors. No spatial or temporal blocking reported in methods. Scripts could not be downloaded, so exact fold code was not inspected.
study_details.external_red_list: 189randomly selected100x100mplots on regular Swiss grid, August–midNovember fruitbody surveys, presence-only. Used to compare slope distributions and evaluate slope-related sampling-bias explanation; not independent validation of predictive TSS, temporal forecasts, or Italian transfer. Raw Red List dataset explicitly not public.
study_details.reported_result: With-soil TSS0.53±0.13overall; relative TSS change by species ranges−4%to31%. Soil contribution11%is variance in habitat suitability, not11percentagepoints of finding probability.
study_details.limitations: Citizen-science sampling bias was not corrected; host information omitted; soil predictors limited. Model comparison intentionally constrained predictors, not best possible predictive model.

envidat.resolution: 25mGeoTIFFs for Swiss forest only, including90%prediction-interval uncertainty maps; not Italian coverage
envidat.schema: SoilMaps_description.xlsx plus seven soil map archives(clay,density,depth,gravel,pH,sand,SOC) and seven uncertainty archives. Six standard depths0–5,5–15,15–30,30–60,60–100,100–200cm, except total depth.

italy_cold_start_inference.usable: Supports including soil pH, SOC, texture, depth and uncertainty alongside climate, topography and host vegetation in a static habitat prior, using legally reusable Italian-coverage layers.
italy_cold_start_inference.not_supported: Swiss raster maps do not cover Italy. Coordinate-stripped CSVs cannot support independent spatial refolding. This study does not calibrate Italian daily fruiting, biomass, availability or search-success probability without Italian observations and effort.
italy_cold_start_inference.validation_needed: Nested spatial/temporal validation, Italian external field observations, explicit searched-but-not-found outings, effort/detection model and calibration. Keep static habitat suitability separate from daily fruiting and finding probability.
italy_cold_start_inference.status: Inference for Fronda architecture; not a finding validated in this paper.
